case_name: Chhotanney and Others v State of Uttar Pradesh and Others

statutes.act: Read With Section 201 And 148 Of The Indian Penal Code

facts: The challenge in this appeal is to the judgment of a Division Bench of the Allahabad High Court dismissing the appeal filed by the appellants and respondents 2 and 3 who were co-accused persons.
On 18.11.1977 one Zahid Khan (hereinafter referred to as the 'deceased') was killed.
The upper portion of the head was missing.
The place of occurrence was a user land having grass on it and a site plan was prepared.
As the accused persons pleaded innocence, trial was held.
It appears that there were three eye witnesses PWs 1, 2 and 3.
issues: Whether the ocular evidence is at variance with the medical evidence?
Whether the injuries could not have been caused by lathis?
Whether the medical evidence is at variance with ocular evidence?
petitioner_arguments: The stand taken by the appellants before the High Court was re-iterated.
It is submitted that PW-3 could not recognize the accused is not factually correct as it is evident from a bare reading of the evidence of PW-3.
It is also submitted that the ocular evidence is at variance with the medical evidence.
The stand that PWs 2 and 3 have not identified the accused persons and the medical evidence was in conflict with the ocular evidence.
respondent_arguments: According to the prosecution, accused Liyakat and Abdullah held lathis.
It was also submitted that according to the prosecution, the dead body was dragged but there was no injury.
court_reasoning: The importance and primacy of the quality of the trial process.

Eye witnesses' account would require a careful independent assessment and evaluation for their credibility which should not be adversely prejudged making any other evidence, including medical evidence, as the sole touchstone for the test of such credibility.
A person has, no doubt, a profound right not to be convicted of an offence which is not established by the evidential standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt.
cases_cited: Chhotanney and Others v State of Uttar Pradesh
J. (as His Lordship then was) in State of U.P. v. Krishna Gopal
